steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Multi-fingered robotic platforms are essential for doing complicated tasks such as fruit harvesting and circuit assembly. But to perform these dexterous manipulation tasks, various challenging factors have to be dealt with, including high-dimensionality, hybrid dynamics and uncertainties about the environment.

So multi-fingered manipulation in deployed systems has unique challenges that practical controllers have to overcome. In our work we give a method for creating controllers that can achieve reliable dexterous manipulation tasks across a variety of domain shifts, both from sim to real and across different simulation scenarios. We show that our system is robust by: showing that policies created in simulation transfer to the real world, varying system parameters and showing robustness, and changing the object that is manipulated.

We train and evaluate our controllers on the TriFinger hand. The Trifinger system has a challenging configuration (the hand is oriented down) and the task is challenging too (grasping and then reposing), but we still train a unified neural-network that achieves effective and robust control over the system.

The Trifinger robots are run as cloud-based robot farms. Remote robotic systems like this promise to remove many of the upfront requirements of installing and maintaining robot hardware. But RaaS systems are also more rigid than the research platforms that are commonly used, because controllers designed for individual platforms have to be rolled out across the whole fleet. So the robustness of our learning-based approach is proven further by deploying it on a system that we did not have physical access to.

The key insight of this paper is a careful integration and evaluation of empirical advances in reinforcement learning with high-speed simulation, and practical deployment on a remote robot system. In particular, the contributions of this robot systems work are:

- 1. We give a framework for learning the skill of in-hand manipulation tasks that is robust to sim-to-real transfer and object morphology.

- 2. Unlike previous in-hand manipulation systems, we produce one single policy that does both grasping and re-posing, which simplifies the pipeline of using RL in these systems.

- 3. We show the benefits of using keypoints to represent the object in RL algorithms for in-hand manipulation, especially for reposing in 6-DoF.

- 4. We show our system is robust to changes in object morphology and physics parameters, with simulated experiments and with demonstrated sim-to-real transfer.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Multi-fingered robotic platforms are essential for executing complicated tasks such as fruit harvesting and circuit assembly. However, performing such dexterous manipulation tasks requires dealing with various challenging factors, including high-dimensionality, hybrid dynamics, and uncertainties about the environment [1].

Therefore, multi-fingered manipulation in the context of deployed systems poses unique challenges which practical controllers must overcome. In our work, we provide a method for creating controllers capable of achieving reliable dexterous manipulation tasks across a variety of domain shifts, both from sim to real and across different simulation scenarios. We demonstrate the robustness of our system by showing transfer of policies created in simulation to the real world, varying system parameters and showing robustness, and changing the object being manipulated.

Our controllers are trained and evaluated on the TriFinger [2] hand. Despite the challenging configuration of the Trifinger system (hand oriented down) and of the task (grasping and subsequent reposing), we train a unified neural-network that achieves effective and robust control over the system.

The Trifinger robots are run as cloud-based robot farms. Such remote robotic systems promise to alleviate many of the upfront requirements of installing and maintaining robot hardware [3]. However, RaaS systems are also more rigid than commonly used research platforms, since controllers designed for individual platforms must be rolled out across the entire fleet. Hence, the robustness of our learning-based approach is further proven by deployment on a system we had no physical access to.

The key insight of this paper lies in a careful integration and evaluation of empirical advances in reinforcement learning with high-speed simulation, and practical deployment on a remote robot system. In particular, the contributions of this robot systems work are:

- 1. We provide a framework for learning the skill of in-hand manipulation tasks that is robust to sim-to-real transfer and object morphology.

- 2. Unlike previous in-hand manipulation systems, we produce a single policy which performs both grasping and re-posing, simplifying the pipeline of using RL in such systems.

- 3. We show the benefits of using keypoints to represent the object in RL algorithms for in-hand manipulation, especially when reposing in 6-DoF.

- 4. We show our system is robust to changing object morphology and physics parameters, through simulated experiments and demonstrated sim-to-real transfer.

References:
[1] A. M. Okamura, N. Smaby, and M. R. Cutkosky, “An overview of dexterous manipulation,” in Proceedings 2000 ICRA. IEEE, 2000.
[2] M. Wüthrich, F. Widmaier, F. Grimminger, J. Akpo, S. Joshi, V. Agrawal, B. Hammoud, M. Khadiv, M. Bogdanovic, V. Berenz, J. Viereck, M. Naveau, L. Righetti, B. Schölkopf, and S. Bauer, “Trifinger: An open-source robot for learning dexterity,” 2020. [Online]. Available: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.03596
[3] B. Kehoe, S. Patil, P. Abbeel, and K. Goldberg, “A survey of research on cloud robotics and automation,” IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering , no. 2, 2015.
